correctness.rationale: For every n>=3,k>=1, the proof establishes |D_i|>=k by a 3(k-1)+2<3k+1 capacity bound. Equality forces one hole per cycle layer, a unique tiling by k disjoint closed neighborhoods, and a coherent orientation of all n connecting edges. This yields an if-and-only-if cyclic step condition with S={2,5,...,3k-1} in Z/(3k+1). The +2 permutation decomposes into orbits of n or n/2. Explicit zero-sum walks of lengths 2 (all k), 5 (k>=3), 7 (k>=2), plus rigorous three-step and k=2 five-step obstructions, classify all feasible orbit lengths. A separate explicit construction produces a dominating set of size kn+1 for every parameter pair and identifies its at most two residual adjacent holes. Thus failure of equality forces kn+1 and all boundaries are covered. The bundled standard-library verifier independently tests graph neighborhoods, the walk classification and lower-bound attainability for 522 pairs, with five small connecting-map censuses; finite checks corroborate but do not prove infinite claims.

originality.rationale: The 2023 preprint and 2024 journal version by Henning, Klavžar, Kleszcz and Pilśniak establish only that the parameter on pairs of cycles of orders n and 3k+1 lies in {kn,kn+1}; they prove equality kn when n is divisible by four, with isolated other examples, and leave the remaining residue families unresolved. The exact classification here has genuine additional cases: for k>=3 all n except 3 and 6 attain kn, whereas n=3,6 cannot. For k=2 the exact excluded orders are 3,5,6,10. The original product paper does not imply these domination values. Searches of the catalog of public research claims and other mathematical literature by invariant, product notation, congruence spectrum, and equivalent closed-walk formulation did not return a theorem implying this classification. That negative search is not proof of historical novelty. An older author-hosted submit-version PDF is indexed with a purported stronger exact expression kn+ceil(n/4)-floor(n/4); this superseded draft expression cannot be a valid covering result, because the explicit n=7,k=3 map f=(0,4,5,6,0,8,2) gives a directly checked dominating set of size 21 on 70 vertices, versus that expression’s value 22. The later freely readable revised version and the published journal version instead print only the two-value range. The earlier full draft was inaccessible and is recorded as a residual comparison risk, not cited as a proof.

value.rationale: This answers the precise natural gap left by the foundational paper: its unresolved choice between kn and kn+1 for all cycles C_n with C_{3k+1}. The complete criterion is structural, not a parameter renaming: sharp domination corresponds to existence of a prescribed zero-sum closed walk, whose full length spectrum has nontrivial exceptional orders. The theorem supplies an unrestricted infinite two-parameter classification and an explicit construction realizing every optimum, including corrections to the earlier sufficient condition for 4|n. It has direct significance for the same invariant on the same family, independent of future generalizations.
